pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review"] O2["Write outputs/pr_review_general.md — brief general PR comment (1-2 paragraphs max)"] O3["Write outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md — …

blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.
- `git commit --no-verify` is a code smell; if you use it, say why in the message.

## 5. Current status & next work

**All 5 phases implemented.** 387 canonical MCP tools across 17 integrations
(no dmtools-agents tool call remains uncovered; the Java↔Dart gap snapshot in
`test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` tracks the remaining non-agent names).
QuickJS runtime via dart:ffi with sync callbacks — dmtools-agents suite passes
unmodified (751 tests green). CliAgent lifecycle fully
ported (incl. timer/error/line JS actions). `dmtools run`, `list`, `doctor`,
`--version`, `--help`, `--list-jobs` all functional.

**Sync dispatch** (`executeToolViaJava`): `SyncToolDispatcher` routes by
prefix to self-contained per-integration classes in `lib/src/js/sync_tools/`
(jira, github, gitlab, ado, confluence, bitrise, jenkins) plus per-provider
`<provider>_ai_chat` — HTTP via curl subprocess inside NativeCallable
callbacks, `file_*`/`cli_*` via `SyncToolDispatcher.nonHttpHandler`. The
JS bridge (`JobJavaScriptBridge` parity): CommonJS `require` loader
(`require_loader.dart`), JSRunner context (`ticket`/`response`/`initiator`/

{"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md","content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Downstream interrupted-rework detection (`isInterruptedReworkResponse`) doesn't know the new failure prefix**

The new always-present marker `CLI command failed (exit code N) …` is not matched by the JS consumers that classify a failed rework:

- `agents/js/pushReworkChanges.js:454` (`isInterruptedReworkResponse`)
- `factory-agents/js/pushReworkChanges.js:435` (same matcher)

Today this works only by accident: `pr_rework.json` has a **single** `cliCommands` entry, so the monitored-path marker `Command failed (exit code 124)` lands at ~char 60 of `commandResponses` and survives inside the 2000-char **head** window of the excerpt. Two gaps remain:

1. **Latent truncation regression** — any future multi-command rework batch where a chatty command precedes the failing one pushes `Command failed (exit code 124)` into the dropped middle. `isInterruptedReworkResponse` then returns `false` and `pushReworkChanges` posts "✅ Rework Completed", moves the ticket to In Review and skips the resume flow — for an interrupted run. The bounded excerpt is exactly the kind of text this matcher must classify, so the matcher should not depend on where in the excerpt a marker happens to land.
2. **Pre-existing gap this change makes trivially fixable** — fatal exits ≠ 124 (provider crash, exit 1/2/7) never matched and are still announced as "Rework Completed". The new stable prefix would close that class.

Note this is load-bearing under the Dart runtime: `params.currentCliHasFatalError` (the authoritative signal `developTicketAndCreatePR.js` prefers) is never set by `CliAgent`, so JS text-sniffing of `params.response` is the *only* failure-classification signal.

Suggested fix (one line in both copies + unit tests):

```js
function isInterruptedReworkResponse(response) {
    var text = String(response || '');
    return text.indexOf('CLI command failed (exit code') !== -1 ||   // NEW — gh-192 prefix
        text.indexOf('CLI command executed but did not produce output file') !== -1 ||
        ...
}
```

and extend `agents/js/unit-tests/test_reworkCustomParams.js` ("detects interrupted pr_rework responses") with the new prefix, e.g. `isInterruptedReworkResponse('CLI command failed (exit code 7) and did not produce response.md …') === true`.
"}

{"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md","content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: Success-path fallback still publishes the unbounded full session log**

`return result.commandResponses;` still returns the **complete** accumulated log when a run exits 0 without writing `response.md` — and post-actions publish `params.response` verbatim. That is the same megabyte-comment failure mode gh-192 fixes, one branch over (e.g. an agent that "succeeds" but skips the output file, or a `skipAIProcessing` job with noisy commands).

Understood that this keeps Java parity (the deviation note above documents the failure-path divergence), but consider at least capping this branch too — e.g. the same `boundedLog` with a larger cap, or a success-specific marker — so no CliAgent response can ever be unbounded. If it's intentionally deferred, a code comment here saying "full log on success is intentional (Java parity)" would prevent the next reader from "fixing" it.
"}

{"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment3.md","content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: `substring` can split a UTF-16 surrogate pair**

`text.substring(0, headLength)` and `text.substring(text.length - tailLength)` cut at arbitrary UTF-16 code-unit offsets. If the boundary lands mid-surrogate-pair (emoji, CJK ext-B chars in a session log), the excerpt contains a lone surrogate, which mangles the posted comment (U+FFFD) and produces technically-invalid `\uD8xx` JSON escapes toward the GitHub API.

Low probability, cheap to harden — back the boundary off to a code-unit boundary:

```dart
final head = text.substring(0, headLength);
final headEnd = head.codeUnits.last >= 0xD800 && head.codeUnits.last <= 0xDBFF
    ? headLength - 1 // drop the orphaned high surrogate
    : headLength;
```

(or use the `characters` package). Splitting mid-line/mid-ANSI-escape is cosmetic by comparison and fine to leave.
"}

{"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment5.md","content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: Pin the monitored-path excerpt contract with a test**

All new tests exercise the buffered path (`executeCommands`). The production rework job (`pr_rework.json`) runs the **monitored** path (`timerJSAction` → `executeCommandsWithCallbacks`), whose `commandResponses` format differs (`Error: Command failed (exit code N): <cmd>\nOutput:\n…`), and the downstream JS detection (`isInterruptedReworkResponse`) depends on `Command failed (exit code 124)` surviving inside the excerpt head. Suggest one test (mirroring `cli_agent_js_actions_test.dart`'s callback setup, or directly on `CliExecutionHelper.executeCommandsWithCallbacks` + the same extraction logic) asserting for a large-output timeout-style failure:

- the bounded response still `contains('Command failed (exit code 124)')` (head-window survival), and
- the middle of the output is dropped.

While there, two cheap boundary cases for `boundedLog`: `log.length == cap` → returned unchanged (no marker), and `log.length == cap + 1` → marker with `truncated 1 characters` (consider singular/plural or rewording, since "1 characters" reads oddly).

# PR Discussion History

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `lib/src/agents/cli_agent.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-22):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Downstream interrupted-rework detection (`isInterruptedReworkResponse`) doesn't know the new failure prefix**

The new always-present marker `CLI command failed (exit code N) …` is not matched by the JS consumers that classify a failed rework:

- `agents/js/pushReworkChanges.js:454` (`isInterruptedReworkResponse`)
- `factory-agents/js/pushReworkChanges.js:435` (same matcher)

Today this works only by accident: `pr_rework.json` has a **single** `cliCommands` entry, so the monitored-path marker `Command failed (exit code 124)` lands at ~char 60 of `commandResponses` and survives inside the 2000-char **head** window of the excerpt. Two gaps remain:

1. **Latent truncation regression** — any future multi-command rework batch where a chatty command precedes the failing one pushes `Command failed (exit code 124)` into the dropped middle. `isInterruptedReworkResponse` then returns `false` and `pushReworkChanges` posts "✅ Rework Completed", moves the ticket to In Review and skips the resume flow — for an interrupted run. The bounded excerpt is exactly the kind of text this matcher must classify, so the matcher should not depend on where in the excerpt a marker happens to land.
2. **Pre-existing gap this change makes trivially fixable** — fatal exits ≠ 124 (provider crash, exit 1/2/7) never matched and are still announced as "Rework Completed". The new stable prefix would close that class.

Note this is load-bearing under the Dart runtime: `params.currentCliHasFatalError` (the authoritative signal `developTicketAndCreatePR.js` prefers) is never set by `CliAgent`, so JS text-sniffing of `params.response` is the *only* failure-classification signal.

Suggested fix (one line in both copies + unit tests):

```js
function isInterruptedReworkResponse(response) {
    var text = String(response || '');
    return text.indexOf('CLI command failed (exit code') !== -1 ||   // NEW — gh-192 prefix
        text.indexOf('CLI command executed but did not produce output file') !== -1 ||
        ...
}
```

and extend `agents/js/unit-tests/test_reworkCustomParams.js` ("detects interrupted pr_rework responses") with the new prefix, e.g. `isInterruptedReworkResponse('CLI command failed (exit code 7) and did not produce response.md …') === true`.

---

### Thread 2 — `lib/src/agents/cli_agent.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-22):
💡 **SUGGESTION: Success-path fallback still publishes the unbounded full session log**

`return result.commandResponses;` still returns the **complete** accumulated log when a run exits 0 without writing `response.md` — and post-actions publish `params.response` verbatim. That is the same megabyte-comment failure mode gh-192 fixes, one branch over (e.g. an agent that "succeeds" but skips the output file, or a `skipAIProcessing` job with noisy commands).

Understood that this keeps Java parity (the deviation note above documents the failure-path divergence), but consider at least capping this branch too — e.g. the same `boundedLog` with a larger cap, or a success-specific marker — so no CliAgent response can ever be unbounded. If it's intentionally deferred, a code comment here saying "full log on success is intentional (Java parity)" would prevent the next reader from "fixing" it.

---

### Thread 3 — `lib/src/agents/cli_execution_helper.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-22):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `substring` can split a UTF-16 surrogate pair**

`text.substring(0, headLength)` and `text.substring(text.length - tailLength)` cut at arbitrary UTF-16 code-unit offsets. If the boundary lands mid-surrogate-pair (emoji, CJK ext-B chars in a session log), the excerpt contains a lone surrogate, which mangles the posted comment (U+FFFD) and produces technically-invalid `\uD8xx` JSON escapes toward the GitHub API.

Low probability, cheap to harden — back the boundary off to a code-unit boundary:

```dart
final head = text.substring(0, headLength);
final headEnd = head.codeUnits.last >= 0xD800 && head.codeUnits.last <= 0xDBFF
    ? headLength - 1 // drop the orphaned high surrogate
    : headLength;
```

(or use the `characters` package). Splitting mid-line/mid-ANSI-escape is cosmetic by comparison and fine to leave.

---

### Thread 4 — `lib/src/agents/cli_agent.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-22):
💡 **SUGGESTION: First doc sentence now contradicts the behavior**

The doc still opens with "Mirrors Java `extractResponse`: … command responses are the fallback", while the deviation paragraph below (correctly) says failed runs return a bounded excerpt instead. Suggest rewording the first paragraph so it stands alone, e.g.:

```dart
/// Mirrors Java `extractResponse`: `requireCliOutputFile` turns a missing
/// output file into an error; the output file content is preferred; command
/// responses are the fallback **for successful runs** (failed runs are
/// bounded — see below).
```

Purely docs, but this method is the failure-publishing contract for every consumer, so the summary sentence should not need the second paragraph to be true.

---

### Thread 5 — `test/agents/cli_failure_response_test.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-22):
💡 **SUGGESTION: Pin the monitored-path excerpt contract with a test**

All new tests exercise the buffered path (`executeCommands`). The production rework job (`pr_rework.json`) runs the **monitored** path (`timerJSAction` → `executeCommandsWithCallbacks`), whose `commandResponses` format differs (`Error: Command failed (exit code N): <cmd>\nOutput:\n…`), and the downstream JS detection (`isInterruptedReworkResponse`) depends on `Command failed (exit code 124)` surviving inside the excerpt head. blocks.text:
name: Quality

# Dispatch-only CI (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes fire NO CI —
# the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger. It dispatches
# this workflow on the PR head when validation is due (sm rule
# validate-fresh / validate-armed), so intermediate dev/rework pushes and
# silent branch updates are free. Required checks still match: the
# dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
# Main keeps its push CI (badges + history).
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch: {}

concurrency:
  # PR branches: a fresh dispatch supersedes the in-flight run. Main keeps
  # every run (badges + history).
  group: quality-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}

jobs:
  static:
    # Fast lane: format + analyze need no toolchain (gcc/QuickJS) — they
    # finish in ~2 min and fail the pipeline early on style/type errors.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get
      - run: dart format --set-exit-if-changed .
      - run: dart analyze

  test:
    # The suite (~2.3k tests) is sharded 4 ways — wall time drops from
    # ~17 min serial to ~5-6 min (fixed per-shard overhead ~3 min +
    # suite/4). Each shard uploads its partial lcov + test count; the
    # gate job merges them.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2, 3]
    env:
      TOTAL_SHARDS: 4
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          # agents/ — the machine-wiring tests (test/machine_kit/) resolve
          # the runner configs' parents under agents/ (a submodule); without
          # the checkout, RunCommandProcessor dies with PathNotFoundException.
          submodules: true
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get
      - name: Install gcc
        run: |
          # apt hung twice on 2026-08-19 (no exit — jobs burned 19+ minutes on
          # this step before manual cancellation). Cap each attempt and retry
          # so a flaky mirror fails the job fast instead of stalling it.
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            if timeout 300 sudo apt-get update -qq && \
               timeout 300 sudo apt-get install -y -qq gcc; then
              exit 0
            fi
            echo "apt attempt $attempt failed or timed out; retrying in 15s"
            sudo dpkg --configure -a || true
            sleep 15
          done
          echo "apt failed after 3 attempts"
          exit 1
      - name: Build QuickJS (quickjs_runtime package)
        run: |
          PKG=$(python3 -c "import json;print([p['rootUri'] for p in json.load(open('.dart_tool/package_config.json'))['packages'] if p['name']=='quickjs_runtime'][0].replace('file://',''))")
          bash "$PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"
      - name: dart test (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/${{ env.TOTAL_SHARDS }}) --coverage
        id: test
        # pipefail keeps a red shard red through the tee; the captured count
        # feeds the badges step (summed across shards in the gate job).
        # --reporter compact: on CI dart test auto-selects the github
        # reporter, which has no +N counters and would leave COUNT empty
        # (grep exits 1, bash -e kills the step).
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          dart test --coverage=coverage --reporter compact \
            --total-shards "$TOTAL_SHARDS" --shard-index "${{ matrix.shard }}" \
            2>&1 | tee /tmp/test_run.log
          COUNT=$(grep -oE '\+[0-9]+' /tmp/test_run.log | tail -1 | tr -d '+' || true)
          echo "test_count=${COUNT:-0}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - run: dart pub global activate coverage
      - name: Format coverage (shard)
        run: |
          dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
            --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: lcov-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 1
      - name: Upload shard test count
        run: echo "${{ steps.test.outputs.test_count }}" > shard_count.txt
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: count-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: shard_count.txt
          retention-days: 1

  gate:
    # Single merge point: full coverage lcov + total test count restored
    # from the shards, then the crap4dart gates and the badges. Required
    # status check — a red shard fails this job through `needs`.
    needs: [static, test]
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          pattern: lcov-*
          path: coverage-shards
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          pattern: count-*
          path: shard-counts
      - name: Merge shard coverage
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update -qq && sudo apt-get install -y -qq lcov
          mkdir -p coverage
          ARGS=$(for f in coverage-shards/lcov-*/lcov.info; do printf -- '-a %s ' "$f"; done)
          # shellcheck disable=SC2086
          lcov $ARGS -o coverage/lcov.info
      - name: Sum shard test counts
        id: counts
        run: |
          TOTAL=$(cat shard-counts/count-*/shard_count.txt | awk '{s+=$1} END{print s+0}')
          echo "test_count=$TOTAL" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - name: Install crap4dart
        # 0.9.5: fixed the test_assertions parser limitation with trailing
        # named `skip:` args, so the two config excludes are gone. Keep this
        # pin aligned with the version the pre-commit hook runs locally.
        run: dart pub global activate crap4dart 0.9.5
      - run: crap4dart check --all
      - run: crap4dart analyze
      - name: Generate badges
        run: |
          mkdir -p .badges
          TEST_COUNT="${{ steps.counts.outputs.test_count }}"
          COV_PCT=$(grep -o 'LH:[0-9]*' coverage/lcov.info | awk -F: '{s+=$2} END{print s}')
          COV_TOTAL=$(grep -o 'LF:[0-9]*' coverage/lcov.info | awk -F: '{s+=$2} END{print s}')
          COV_FINAL=$(echo "scale=1; $COV_PCT * 100 / $COV_TOTAL" | bc 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
          CRAP="8.0"

          # shields.io flakes (503/connection blips) must not red the whole
          # pipeline — badges are cosmetic. Retry, then warn and move on
          # (the commit step already tolerates missing files).
          fetch_badge() {
            local url="$1" out="$2" attempt
            for attempt in 1 2 3; do
              if wget -q -O "$out" "$url"; then return 0; fi
              sleep 5
            done
            echo "::warning::badge fetch failed after 3 attempts: $url"
          }

          # Tests badge
          fetch_badge \
            "https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-${TEST_COUNT}%20passing-brightgreen" \
            .badges/tests.svg
          # Coverage badge
          fetch_badge \
            "https://img.shields.io/badge/coverage-${COV_FINAL}%25-brightgreen" \
            .badges/coverage.svg
          # crap4dart badge
          fetch_badge \
            "https://img.shields.io/badge/crap4dart-${CRAP}%20threshold-green" \
            .badges/crap4dart.svg
      - name: Commit badges
        # Badges belong to main only — on PR branches this step would push a
        # stray bot commit to the feature branch mid-review.
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
        run: |
          git config user.name 'github-actions[bot]'
          git config user.email 'github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com'
          git add .badges/*.svg || true
          git diff --staged --quiet || git commit -m 'chore: update CI badges [skip ci]'
          git push || true

  agents-suite:
    # Runs in parallel with the test shards — both are required merge checks
    # and the suite hard-gates on its own, so serializing only adds wall time.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

- **static**: `dart format --set-exit-if-changed .` + `dart analyze` (whole repo)
- **test**: 4 shards of `dart test --coverage` (one shard "test (3)" = shard index 3 failed... "test (3)" in the failure list — GitHub displays matrix as "test (3)" meaning shard 3)
- **gate**: needs [static, test] — fails transitively when static or test fails
- **agents-suite**: `dart run bin/run_agents_suite.dart agents` — the L4 JS suite

So the failed checks: static ❌, gate ❌ (transitive via needs), test (3) ❌, agents-suite ❌ ×2 (two different workflow runs: 35697186609 and 35697556366).

Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review"] O2["Write outputs/pr_review_general.md — brief general PR comment (1-2 paragraphs max)"] O3["Write outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md — …

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.
- `git commit --no-verify` is a code smell; if you use it, say why in the message.

## 5. Current status & next work

**All 5 phases implemented.** 387 canonical MCP tools across 17 integrations
(no dmtools-agents tool call remains uncovered; the Java↔Dart gap snapshot in
`test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` tracks the remaining non-agent names).
QuickJS runtime via dart:ffi with sync callbacks — dmtools-agents suite passes
unmodified (751 tests green). CliAgent lifecycle fully
ported (incl. timer/error/line JS actions). `dmtools run`, `list`, `doctor`,
`--version`, `--help`, `--list-jobs` all functional.

**Sync dispatch** (`executeToolViaJava`): `SyncToolDispatcher` routes by
prefix to self-contained per-integration classes in `lib/src/js/sync_tools/`
(jira, github, gitlab, ado, confluence, bitrise, jenkins) plus per-provider
`<provider>_ai_chat` — HTTP via curl subprocess inside NativeCallable
callbacks, `file_*`/`cli_*` via `SyncToolDispatcher.nonHttpHandler`. The
JS bridge (`JobJavaScriptBridge` parity): CommonJS `require` loader
(`require_loader.dart`), JSRunner context (`ticket`/`response`/`initiator`/
`inputJql`/`metadata`), inline/URL/file jsPath, action() contract, JS-visible
host-fn validation errors (`__jsError` sentinel), alias tool wrappers.

**Remaining work** (diminishing returns, in priority order):
1. InstructionProcessor
2. Integration test layer (L2 contract tests, L3 live integration)
3. Re-extract `test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_names.txt` when Java gains new
   @MCPTools and port what the gap snapshot then reports

Phase checkboxes live in GOAL.md — tick them as you complete items and keep the
file current when a decision changes the plan.

## 6. Testing layers (so you put each test in the right place)

| Layer | Location | Runs where |
|---|---|---|
| L1 unit | `test/`, mocked | pre-commit + CI quality.yml |
| L2 contract | `test/` with recorded Java fixtures | CI quality.yml |
| L3 live integration | `test/` `@Tags(['integration'])`, creds via env/`dmtools.env` | nightly + manual, excluded by default via `dart_test.yaml` |
| L4 agents suite | external `agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` | dedicated CI job from Phase 4 |

The agents suite (`dmtools run agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` under the Dart
runtime, unmodified) is the **primary acceptance gate** — see GOAL.md.

## 7. Style notes

- `dart format` defaults; public API documented (public_docs gate enforces it).
- Keep methods small (complexity ≤ 10, body ≤ 60 lines, params ≤ 6 — the gates
  enforce this; design around it rather than fighting it).
- Generated code (`*.g.dart`, `*.freezed.dart`) is gate-excluded by default —
  don't hand-edit, regenerate.

## 8. fa session reuse (CI machine)

The ai-teammate machine resumes one fa session per ticket instead of starting
cold on every run. Sessions are named deterministically per `repo:GH-<n>:group` —
bug/story/rework share the `dev-write` conversation (a rework continues the
ticket's dev thread), review has its own `dev-review`. The session directory
(`.dmtools/fa-sessions`) travels across CI runs on a dedicated per-issue branch
`fa-sess/gh-<n>`: restored before the run, force-pushed after it, never merged.
For live debugging, `FA_LOG_FILE` (`fa --log-file`) captures the full
untruncated agent transcript, uploaded as the `fa-trace-*` run artifact;
dmtools also streams the agent's output live into the step log via stderr
mirroring (gh-50). Wiring: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`.

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #203._

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `lib/src/agents/cli_agent.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-22):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Downstream interrupted-rework detection (`isInterruptedReworkResponse`) doesn't know the new failure prefix**

The new always-present marker `CLI command failed (exit code N) …` is not matched by the JS consumers that classify a failed rework:

- `agents/js/pushReworkChanges.js:454` (`isInterruptedReworkResponse`)
- `factory-agents/js/pushReworkChanges.js:435` (same matcher)

Today this works only by accident: `pr_rework.json` has a **single** `cliCommands` entry, so the monitored-path marker `Command failed (exit code 124)` lands at ~char 60 of `commandResponses` and survives inside the 2000-char **head** window of the excerpt. Two gaps remain:

1. **Latent truncation regression** — any future multi-command rework batch where a chatty command precedes the failing one pushes `Command failed (exit code 124)` into the dropped middle. `isInterruptedReworkResponse` then returns `false` and `pushReworkChanges` posts "✅ Rework Completed", moves the ticket to In Review and skips the resume flow — for an interrupted run. The bounded excerpt is exactly the kind of text this matcher must classify, so the matcher should not depend on where in the excerpt a marker happens to land.
2. **Pre-existing gap this change makes trivially fixable** — fatal exits ≠ 124 (provider crash, exit 1/2/7) never matched and are still announced as "Rework Completed". The new stable prefix would close that class.

Note this is load-bearing under the Dart runtime: `params.currentCliHasFatalError` (the authoritative signal `developTicketAndCreatePR.js` prefers) is never set by `CliAgent`, so JS text-sniffing of `params.response` is the *only* failure-classification signal.

Suggested fix (one line in both copies + unit tests):

```js
function isInterruptedReworkResponse(response) {
    var text = String(response || '');
    return text.indexOf('CLI command failed (exit code') !== -1 ||   // NEW — gh-192 prefix
        text.indexOf('CLI command executed but did not produce output file') !== -1 ||
        ...
}
```

and extend `agents/js/unit-tests/test_reworkCustomParams.js` ("detects interrupted pr_rework responses") with the new prefix, e.g. `isInterruptedReworkResponse('CLI command failed (exit code 7) and did not produce response.md …') === true`.

---

### Thread 2 — `lib/src/agents/cli_agent.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-22):
💡 **SUGGESTION: Success-path fallback still publishes the unbounded full session log**

`return result.commandResponses;` still returns the **complete** accumulated log when a run exits 0 without writing `response.md` — and post-actions publish `params.response` verbatim. That is the same megabyte-comment failure mode gh-192 fixes, one branch over (e.g. an agent that "succeeds" but skips the output file, or a `skipAIProcessing` job with noisy commands).

Understood that this keeps Java parity (the deviation note above documents the failure-path divergence), but consider at least capping this branch too — e.g. the same `boundedLog` with a larger cap, or a success-specific marker — so no CliAgent response can ever be unbounded. If it's intentionally deferred, a code comment here saying "full log on success is intentional (Java parity)" would prevent the next reader from "fixing" it.

---

### Thread 3 — `lib/src/agents/cli_execution_helper.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-22):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `substring` can split a UTF-16 surrogate pair**

`text.substring(0, headLength)` and `text.substring(text.length - tailLength)` cut at arbitrary UTF-16 code-unit offsets. If the boundary lands mid-surrogate-pair (emoji, CJK ext-B chars in a session log), the excerpt contains a lone surrogate, which mangles the posted comment (U+FFFD) and produces technically-invalid `\uD8xx` JSON escapes toward the GitHub API.

Low probability, cheap to harden — back the boundary off to a code-unit boundary:

```dart
final head = text.substring(0, headLength);
final headEnd = head.codeUnits.last >= 0xD800 && head.codeUnits.last <= 0xDBFF
    ? headLength - 1 // drop the orphaned high surrogate
    : headLength;
```

(or use the `characters` package). Splitting mid-line/mid-ANSI-escape is cosmetic by comparison and fine to leave.

---

### Thread 4 — `lib/src/agents/cli_agent.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-22):
💡 **SUGGESTION: First doc sentence now contradicts the behavior**

The doc still opens with "Mirrors Java `extractResponse`: … command responses are the fallback", while the deviation paragraph below (correctly) says failed runs return a bounded excerpt instead. Suggest rewording the first paragraph so it stands alone, e.g.:

```dart
/// Mirrors Java `extractResponse`: `requireCliOutputFile` turns a missing
/// output file into an error; the output file content is preferred; command
/// responses are the fallback **for successful runs** (failed runs are
/// bounded — see below).
```

Purely docs, but this method is the failure-publishing contract for every consumer, so the summary sentence should not need the second paragraph to be true.

---

### Thread 5 — `test/agents/cli_failure_response_test.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-22):
💡 **SUGGESTION: Pin the monitored-path excerpt contract with a test**

All new tests exercise the buffered path (`executeCommands`). The production rework job (`pr_rework.json`) runs the **monitored** path (`timerJSAction` → `executeCommandsWithCallbacks`), whose `commandResponses` format differs (`Error: Command failed (exit code N): <cmd>\nOutput:\n…`), and the downstream JS detection (`isInterruptedReworkResponse`) depends on `Command failed (exit code 124)` surviving inside the excerpt head. A regression here wouldn't be caught by this suite.

Suggest one test (mirroring `cli_agent_js_actions_test.dart`'s callback setup, or directly on `CliExecutionHelper.executeCommandsWithCallbacks` + the same extraction logic) asserting for a large-output timeout-style failure:

- the bounded response still `contains('Command failed (exit code 124)')` (head-window survival), and
- the middle of the output is dropped.

While there, two cheap boundary cases for `boundedLog`: `log.length == cap` → returned unchanged (no marker), and `log.length == cap + 1` → marker with `truncated 1 characters` (consider singular/plural or rewording, since "1 characters" reads oddly).

---

### Thread 6

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-22):
## Automated Code Review — APPROVE

**Summary**: The gh-192 fix is correct, well-placed, and well-tested: `_extractResponse` is the single choke point (verified — `TeammateJob` delegates to `CliAgent`), success paths and the `requireCliOutputFile` marker are preserved verbatim, and the new tests pass (7/7; full `test/agents/` 160/160; `dart analyze` + format clean). One important follow-up: the vendored JS consumer `isInterruptedReworkResponse` was not taught the new `CLI command failed (exit code` prefix, so interrupted-rework classification still leans on the old `Command failed (exit code 124)` marker surviving in the excerpt head window.

2. 💡 Success-without-`response.md` still publishes the unbounded full log (documented as deliberate Java parity — please mark it with a comment)

2. Optionally: cap the success fallback, harden `boundedLog` boundaries, add the monitored-path regression test

blocks.text:
name: Quality

# Dispatch-only CI (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes fire NO CI —
# the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger. It dispatches
# this workflow on the PR head when validation is due (sm rule
# validate-fresh / validate-armed), so intermediate dev/rework pushes and
# silent branch updates are free. Required checks still match: the
# dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
# Main keeps its push CI (badges + history).
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch: {}

concurrency:
  # PR branches: a fresh dispatch supersedes the in-flight run. Main keeps
  # every run (badges + history).
  group: quality-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}

jobs:
  static:
    # Fast lane: format + analyze need no toolchain (gcc/QuickJS) — they
    # finish in ~2 min and fail the pipeline early on style/type errors.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get
      - run: dart format --set-exit-if-changed .
      - run: dart analyze

  test:
    # The suite (~2.3k tests) is sharded 4 ways — wall time drops from
    # ~17 min serial to ~5-6 min (fixed per-shard overhead ~3 min +
    # suite/4). Each shard uploads its partial lcov + test count; the
    # gate job merges them.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2, 3]
    env:
      TOTAL_SHARDS: 4
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          # agents/ — the machine-wiring tests (test/machine_kit/) resolve
          # the runner configs' parents under agents/ (a submodule); without
          # the checkout, RunCommandProcessor dies with PathNotFoundException.
          submodules: true
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get
      - name: Install gcc
        run: |
          # apt hung twice on 2026-08-19 (no exit — jobs burned 19+ minutes on
          # this step before manual cancellation). Cap each attempt and retry
          # so a flaky mirror fails the job fast instead of stalling it.
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            if timeout 300 sudo apt-get update -qq && \
               timeout 300 sudo apt-get install -y -qq gcc; then
              exit 0
            fi
            echo "apt attempt $attempt failed or timed out; retrying in 15s"
            sudo dpkg --configure -a || true
            sleep 15
          done
          echo "apt failed after 3 attempts"
          exit 1
      - name: Build QuickJS (quickjs_runtime package)
        run: |
          PKG=$(python3 -c "import json;print([p['rootUri'] for p in json.load(open('.dart_tool/package_config.json'))['packages'] if p['name']=='quickjs_runtime'][0].replace('file://',''))")
          bash "$PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"
      - name: dart test (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/${{ env.TOTAL_SHARDS }}) --coverage
        id: test
        # pipefail keeps a red shard red through the tee; the captured count
        # feeds the badges step (summed across shards in the gate job).
        # --reporter compact: on CI dart test auto-selects the github
        # reporter, which has no +N counters and would leave COUNT empty
        # (grep exits 1, bash -e kills the step).
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          dart test --coverage=coverage --reporter compact \
            --total-shards "$TOTAL_SHARDS" --shard-index "${{ matrix.shard }}" \
            2>&1 | tee /tmp/test_run.log
          COUNT=$(grep -oE '\+[0-9]+' /tmp/test_run.log | tail -1 | tr -d '+' || true)
          echo "test_count=${COUNT:-0}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - run: dart pub global activate coverage
      - name: Format coverage (shard)
        run: |
          dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
            --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: lcov-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: coverage/lcov.info
          retention-days: 1
      - name: Upload shard test count
        run: echo "${{ steps.test.outputs.test_count }}" > shard_count.txt
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: count-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: shard_count.txt
          retention-days: 1

  gate:
    # Single merge point: full coverage lcov + total test count restored
    # from the shards, then the crap4dart gates and the badges. Required
    # status check — a red shard fails this job through `needs`.
    needs: [static, test]
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          pattern: lcov-*
          path: coverage-shards
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          pattern: count-*
          path: shard-counts
      - name: Merge shard coverage
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update -qq && sudo apt-get install -y -qq lcov
          mkdir -p coverage
          ARGS=$(for f in coverage-shards/lcov-*/lcov.info; do printf -- '-a %s ' "$f"; done)
          # shellcheck disable=SC2086
          lcov $ARGS -o coverage/lcov.info
      - name: Sum shard test counts
        id: counts
        run: |
          TOTAL=$(cat shard-counts/count-*/shard_count.txt | awk '{s+=$1} END{print s+0}')
          echo "test_count=$TOTAL" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - name: Install crap4dart

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,

pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.
- `git commit --no-verify` is a code smell; if you use it, say why in the message.

## 5. Current status & next work

**All 5 phases implemented.** 387 canonical MCP tools across 17 integrations
(no dmtools-agents tool call remains uncovered; the Java↔Dart gap snapshot in
`test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` tracks the remaining non-agent names).
QuickJS runtime via dart:ffi with sync callbacks — dmtools-agents suite passes
unmodified (751 tests green). CliAgent lifecycle fully
ported (incl. timer/error/line JS actions). `dmtools run`, `list`, `doctor`,
`--version`, `--help`, `--list-jobs` all functional.

**Sync dispatch** (`executeToolViaJava`): `SyncToolDispatcher` routes by
prefix to self-contained per-integration classes in `lib/src/js/sync_tools/`
(jira, github, gitlab, ado, confluence, bitrise, jenkins) plus per-provider
`<provider>_ai_chat` — HTTP via curl subprocess inside NativeCallable
callbacks, `file_*`/`cli_*` via `SyncToolDispatcher.nonHttpHandler`. The
JS bridge (`JobJavaScriptBridge` parity): CommonJS `require` loader
(`require_loader.dart`), JSRunner context (`ticket`/`response`/`initiator`/
`inputJql`/`metadata`), inline/URL/file jsPath, action() contract, JS-visible
host-fn validation errors (`__jsError` sentinel), alias tool wrappers.

**Remaining work** (diminishing returns, in priority order):
1. InstructionProcessor
2. Integration test layer (L2 contract tests, L3 live integration)
3. Re-extract `test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_names.txt` when Java gains new
   @MCPTools and port what the gap snapshot then reports

Phase checkboxes live in GOAL.md — tick them as you complete items and keep the
file current when a decision changes the plan.

## 6. Testing layers (so you put each test in the right place)

| Layer | Location | Runs where |
|---|---|---|
| L1 unit | `test/`, mocked | pre-commit + CI quality.yml |
| L2 contract | `test/` with recorded Java fixtures | CI quality.yml |
| L3 live integration | `test/` `@Tags(['integration'])`, creds via env/`dmtools.env` | nightly + manual, excluded by default via `dart_test.yaml` |
| L4 agents suite | external `agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` | dedicated CI job from Phase 4 |

The agents suite (`dmtools run agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` under the Dart
runtime, unmodified) is the **primary acceptance gate** — see GOAL.md.

## 7. Style notes

- `dart format` defaults; public API documented (public_docs gate enforces it).
- Keep methods small (complexity ≤ 10, body ≤ 60 lines, params ≤ 6 — the gates
  enforce this; design around it rather than fighting it).
- Generated code (`*.g.dart`, `*.freezed.dart`) is gate-excluded by default —
  don't hand-edit, regenerate.

## 8. fa session reuse (CI machine)

The ai-teammate machine resumes one fa session per ticket instead of starting
cold on every run. Sessions are named deterministically per `repo:GH-<n>:group` —
bug/story/rework share the `dev-write` conversation (a rework continues the
ticket's dev thread), review has its own `dev-review`. The session directory
(`.dmtools/fa-sessions`) travels across CI runs on a dedicated per-issue branch
`fa-sess/gh-<n>`: restored before the run, force-pushed after it, never merged.
For live debugging, `FA_LOG_FILE` (`fa --log-file`) captures the full
untruncated agent transcript, uploaded as the `fa-trace-*` run artifact;
dmtools also streams the agent's output live into the step log via stderr
mirroring (gh-50). Wiring: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`.

If the log is huge, head=2000 chars keeps the *first* commands, tail=2000 chars keeps the end — the error line `'Command failed (exit code 124): ...'` would be within the last 2000 chars only if the output after it is < ~2000 chars. The bounded excerpt is exactly the kind of text this matcher must classify, so the matcher should not depend on where in the excerpt a marker happens to land.
2. **Pre-existing gap this change makes trivially fixable** — fatal exits ≠ 124 (provider crash, exit 1/2/7) never matched and are still announced as "Rework Completed". The new stable prefix would close that class.

    var text = String(response || '');
    return text.indexOf('CLI command failed (exit code') !== -1 ||   // NEW — gh-192 prefix
        text.indexOf('CLI command executed but did not produce output file') !== -1 ||
        ...
}

{"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment3.md","content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: `substring` can split a UTF-16 surrogate pair**

`text.substring(0, headLength)` and `text.substring(text.length - tailLength)` cut at arbitrary UTF-16 code-unit offsets. If the boundary lands mid-surrogate-pair (emoji, CJK ext-B chars in a session log), the excerpt contains a lone surrogate, which mangles the posted comment (U+FFFD) and produces technically-invalid `\uD8xx` JSON escapes toward the GitHub API.

Low probability, cheap to harden — back the boundary off to a code-unit boundary:

```dart
final head = text.substring(0, headLength);

# PR Discussion History

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `lib/src/agents/cli_agent.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-22):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Downstream interrupted-rework detection (`isInterruptedReworkResponse`) doesn't know the new failure prefix**

The new always-present marker `CLI command failed (exit code N) …` is not matched by the JS consumers that classify a failed rework:

- `agents/js/pushReworkChanges.js:454` (`isInterruptedReworkResponse`)
- `factory-agents/js/pushReworkChanges.js:435` (same matcher)

Today this works only by accident: `pr_rework.json` has a **single** `cliCommands` entry, so the monitored-path marker `Command failed (exit code 124)` lands at ~char 60 of `commandResponses` and survives inside the 2000-char **head** window of the excerpt. Two gaps remain:

1. **Latent truncation regression** — any future multi-command rework batch where a chatty command precedes the failing one pushes `Command failed (exit code 124)` into the dropped middle. `isInterruptedReworkResponse` then returns `false` and `pushReworkChanges` posts "✅ Rework Completed", moves the ticket to In Review and skips the resume flow — for an interrupted run. The bounded excerpt is exactly the kind of text this matcher must classify, so the matcher should not depend on where in the excerpt a marker happens to land.
2. **Pre-existing gap this change makes trivially fixable** — fatal exits ≠ 124 (provider crash, exit 1/2/7) never matched and are still announced as "Rework Completed". The new stable prefix would close that class.

Note this is load-bearing under the Dart runtime: `params.currentCliHasFatalError` (the authoritative signal `developTicketAndCreatePR.js` prefers) is never set by `CliAgent`, so JS text-sniffing of `params.response` is the *only* failure-classification signal.

Suggested fix (one line in both copies + unit tests):

```js
function isInterruptedReworkResponse(response) {
    var text = String(response || '');
    return text.indexOf('CLI command failed (exit code') !== -1 ||   // NEW — gh-192 prefix

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-22):
💡 **SUGGESTION: Success-path fallback still publishes the unbounded full session log**

`return result.commandResponses;` still returns the **complete** accumulated log when a run exits 0 without writing `response.md` — and post-actions publish `params.response` verbatim. ### Thread 3 — `lib/src/agents/cli_execution_helper.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-22):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `substring` can split a UTF-16 surrogate pair**

`text.substring(0, headLength)` and `text.substring(text.length - tailLength)` cut at arbitrary UTF-16 code-unit offsets. If the boundary lands mid-surrogate-pair (emoji, CJK ext-B chars in a session log), the excerpt contains a lone surrogate, which mangles the posted comment (U+FFFD) and produces technically-invalid `\uD8xx` JSON escapes toward the GitHub API.

Low probability, cheap to harden — back the boundary off to a code-unit boundary:

```dart
final head = text.substring(0, headLength);
final headEnd = head.codeUnits.last >= 0xD800 && head.codeUnits.last <= 0xDBFF
    ? headLength - 1 // drop the orphaned high surrogate
    : headLength;
```

(or use the `characters` package). Splitting mid-line/mid-ANSI-escape is cosmetic by comparison and fine to leave.

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-22):

```
